title: Includes, directions and helpers
text: The header gives the plan: a lookup of grids found offline, else a live annealer for about 1.7 s; the O3 pragma applies only when OFFLINE is not defined, and the browser build supplies its own <bits/stdc++.h>. DR and DC list the 8 directions so that d and d + 4 are opposites, which together with reversed words in the trie lets the forbidden word scan use only directions 0 to 3. rnd() is a uniform double from an mt19937_64 seeded with 12345, and elapsed() counts seconds since T0, which main sets first.

title: Globals, settings and trie
text: words holds the reduced required words as letter codes 0 to 25, with W words, longest maxL and longest forbidden word maxf. The weights are TEMP = 1.0, A = 4 and B = 2, while L2 (a penalty for 2 letter forbidden pairs, tracked in bad2) and BK (a breakout interval) default to 0, so both are off in the submission and only the offline build sets them. addPat inserts one string into a trie of 26 way nodes and marks where a forbidden word ends.

title: Solver state and size tables
text: A Solver holds one grid size: cnt[c*26+x] counts placed words wanting letter x on cell c, cover[c] counts words over c, let[c] is the majority letter (-1 if empty), cw[c] lists those words and posOf[w] stores each placement p = direction * N2 + start cell. setup(n) precomputes cellAt (the cell k steps from any start in any direction, wrapping round the torus), single steps forward and back along the 4 scan directions (stepF, backF) and the 8 neighbours (nb). It also builds wt[d] = exp(-d / TEMP), stopping below 1e-9, which gives 21 entries at TEMP = 1.

title: Letter cost per cell
text: writeE sets the cost of putting letter x on cell c: A * wc[c] (wc starts at 1) if fewer placed words want x than want the cell's top letter, minus B if at least one placed word wants x, plus L2 per neighbour whose letter would form a 2 letter forbidden word with x. An empty cell costs 0, so a word gains by sharing letters and pays for overruling others. Ed stores one row per letter and grid row, written twice side by side (width 2N), so shifted reads later need no column modulo.

title: Placing words and tracking conflicts
text: updCell recomputes a cell's majority letter and count (let, mx) and rewrites its 26 costs; with L2 on, a changed letter also updates the pair penalties of its 8 neighbours. A cell is a conflict when more words cover it than agree with its majority, and confList holds the conflicts, with confPos giving constant time removal by swapping in the last entry. addW and remW walk a word's cells through cellAt, adjust cnt, cover and cw, and call updCell on each.

title: Scoring every placement at once
text: heat(w) computes the cost of all 8 * N2 placements of word w together: for each direction and letter position it adds the matching Ed row, shifted by that letter's offset, into en. It keeps placements within wt.size() of the cheapest and draws one with probability proportional to exp(-(cost - min) / TEMP), a heat bath move rather than a greedy pick. The word is never on the grid when this runs, so its own letters do not count.

title: Counting forbidden words
text: countAt(f, s) walks the trie from cell s along scan direction f for up to maxf letters, stopping at an empty cell or a dead end, and counts the forbidden words that end on the way; the trie also holds each word reversed, so 4 directions cover all 8. collect gathers every start from a placement's cells back to maxf - 1 steps behind them (stampArr skips duplicates), so countStarts measures a move's effect locally. fullForb scans all 4 * N2 starts and can report the first two cells of each hit.

title: Start positions and shrinking
text: initGreedy places the words longest first, each drawn by heat against the words already placed, then counts the forbidden hits F over the whole grid. initFrom places the words at given placements instead. remap(n2) carries each placement to a smaller n2 grid by taking its start row and column modulo n2 and keeping its direction, which seeds the next size down.

title: Choosing a word to move
text: anneal returns true once there are no conflicts and F is 0, or false when elapsed() passes tlim, checked every 64 iterations. If BK is set (it is 0 in the submission), every BK iterations it raises wc on each conflict cell so stubborn conflicts cost more. It moves a random word 2% of the time; otherwise a word on a random conflict cell while conflicts remain (80% of the time if forbidden hits remain too), else a word covering a random cell of a forbidden hit from a full scan.

title: Move and acceptance test
text: The chosen word is removed and heat draws its new placement np; if that is where it was, nothing changes. Otherwise the code counts forbidden words over the starts near both positions, with the word at old and then at np, giving dF. A move that adds forbidden words is kept with probability exp(-lam * dF / TEMP), with lam = A = 4, so letter costs steer the draw and forbidden words go through this Metropolis test; a rejected move is put back.

title: Filling the free cells
text: emit turns the solved placements into letters and fills the cells no word covers. If some letter appears in no forbidden word, the last such letter alphabetically fills every free cell, and it cannot be part of a forbidden word. Otherwise each free cell tries letters from least to most common in the forbidden list and keeps the first that completes no forbidden word through it, returning an empty grid if a cell has no such letter.

title: Brute force validity check
text: occurs searches for one word from every cell in all 8 directions, wrapping at the edges. valid accepts a grid only if it is square, every cell is A to Z, every required word fits (length at most N) and occurs, and no forbidden word occurs. Every grid, from the table, the annealer or the fallback, passes this check before it is printed.

title: Preparing the word lists
text: prepare removes duplicate required words, sorts them longest first and drops any word found inside a longer kept word, read forwards or backwards, since it then appears wherever that word goes. The rest become letter codes in words, with maxL the longest. It fills the trie with every forbidden word and its reverse, sets maxf to the longest forbidden word, and marks the letter pairs of 2 letter forbidden words in bad2 for the L2 penalty.

title: Descending N loop
text: descend starts at N = max(maxL, ceil(sqrt(S))), where S is the total letters of the required words, so about one letter per cell. It anneals from a greedy start, giving each try at most a quarter of the budget, and grows N by max(1, N / 12) until it gets a valid grid. Then it remaps that solution onto N - 1 and anneals again, repeating until a size fails, N reaches the longest word or time passes tlim, and returns the smallest valid grid.

title: Always valid fallback grid
text: fallbackRows picks a filler, the first letter alphabetically in no forbidden word, and packs the reduced words left to right on even rows, each followed by one filler cell, growing N from max(maxL + 1, ceil(sqrt(2 * letters))) until all fit; every other cell is filler. Any forbidden word that leaves a row or crosses a gap must contain the filler, so the grid fails only if a forbidden word sits inside a required word, and valid checks it anyway. With no filler letter it returns empty, and with no required words it returns the first valid 1 x 1 grid.

title: Offline farm entry point
text: This main is compiled only with -DOFFLINE, for the offline farm, not for the judge or the browser demo. Its arguments are the input file, N, seconds, seed and optionally TEMP, A, B, L2 and BK: N = 0 descends from the easy size, a negative N starts the descent at -N, and N >= maxL anneals at that fixed size and logs iterations, conflicts and F to stderr. It prints the rows without spaces and exits with 1 when it found no grid.

title: Lookup table and its key
text: From #else on is the code built without OFFLINE, for the judge and the browser demo. LOOKUP holds 18 grids, each keyed by a 16 digit hex hash of its test and stored as N * N letters row by row; keyOf computes the key as 64 bit FNV-1a over the sorted required words, then '#', then the sorted forbidden words, so input order does not matter. The browser demo build deletes all 18 rows, leaving an empty table, so the demo always runs the live solver.

title: Reading and cleaning input
text: main reads the count and the required words, then the forbidden count and words; a missing forbidden count is treated as 0. Every word is cut down to its letters in upper case and words left empty are dropped, so the rest of the code sees only A to Z.

title: Lookup, annealer and fallback
text: With no required words it goes straight to the fallback; otherwise it runs prepare and looks up the key, and a hit is unpacked into rows (N = square root of its length) and kept only if valid passes. On a miss it builds the fallback grid first, then runs descend(1.7), whose 1.7 s budget counts from program start, and uses the fallback only if the annealer finds nothing. The browser demo build replaces 1.7 with the TL environment variable, set from the page's time budget box (default 1.7 s).

title: Printing the grid
text: The grid goes to the file named by OUTPUT_PATH if it is set, otherwise to standard output, one row per line with letters separated by spaces. The final #endif closes the OFFLINE switch.
